reasoning: Palestinian says wisikh with two kasras, not MSA wasikh. Everyday adjective for dirty.
خلّى with shadda doubles the l; the -iik ending is the m. object suffix. خير is kheer with long ee in Palestinian, not khayr.
هيك is heek with long ee. The article assimilates to the sun letter د: id-dinya. Common Palestinian resignation formula.
The -lk cluster holds without an epenthetic vowel, as in mulk. Some speakers do say silik; hence medium.
Word-initial hamza on an alif seat is not written, so just the long vowel: oof. Everyday sigh of exasperation in Ramallah.
Form V verbal noun, shadda on ن doubles it. MSA-origin but it is the word Palestinians actually use when talking about adoption; register is formal.
Shadda on the ya doubles it: nayy. Used of raw meat and undercooked food.
ع is the reduced form of على, fused with the article. Both the hamza after the article and the glottalised ق are written, and the shadda doubles the l.
Literally nostril, but mankhaar is the ordinary Palestinian word for nose; anf is MSA only.
Taa marbuta after م is e. Primary sense is darkness; 3a l-3atme means after dark, which covers the late-night gloss.

meaning_fix: beans (green beans are faaSuulya khaDra; the white bean stew is faaSuulya bayDa)
reasoning: ص is emphatic, so capital S. On its own the word means beans generically; the colour adjective picks out green beans.
The final ـاة is a long aa. MSA-origin abstract noun with no colloquial rival, and it is used in Ramallah talk about rights.
The letter names alif and baa, said as a unit for the ABCs. Initial hamza seat is not written.
ط is emphatic, so capital T. Taa marbuta after ب is e: khaTiibe.
Verbal negation with ما plus the b-prefix: ma biSiir. In fast speech the article vowel elides to illa l-kheer, but the article is kept as il- here.
English loanword, said with two long u vowels and a final th that speakers keep from the source word. Used as-is in Ramallah.
heel with long ee is understood and used, but at a Ramallah spice shop the usual word for cardamom is 7abbahaan.
عمل past 1sg is 3amalt. حادث is a learned borrowing, so its ث comes out as s in urban Palestinian, hence the respelling حادِس; some speakers keep 7aadith.
جامعة loses the short i in Palestinian: jaam3a, with taa marbuta after ع as a. أي is ayy with a doubled ya.
ض is emphatic, so capital D. Taa marbuta after ف is e. Everyday in karam iD-Diyaafe.
ث in this inherited numeral is a plain t in Palestinian, so the Arabic is respelled تلاتين to match talaatiin.

vowelled_arabic: اللي بِحْفُر حُفْرَة لَأَخُو بِيقَع فِيها
reasoning: Relative اللي plus b-prefixed present: bi7fur, bii'a3. ق is glottal in bii'a3, and حفرة takes a after ر. The 3ms possessive on أخو is just a long uu, no final h.
Palestinian has marwa7a with a first fatha, not MSA mirwa7a. The pharyngeal ح backs the taa marbuta to a.
With the article the initial i of إتنين drops and the article assimilates to the sun letter ت: yoom it-tneen. Respelled without the alif-hamza to match that.
Said as in MSA, mahrajaan, and genuinely used in Ramallah for festivals such as mahrajaan Falasteen.
